rounds.fact: Fark built its entire identity around submitting and voting on weird, funny news links, a simple format that predated Reddit's rise by several years.
Circuit City was one of the largest electronics retailers in the US before going bankrupt in 2008, a collapse often cited alongside the rise of Best Buy and online shopping.
Gizmodo's early scoops on unreleased Apple products, sometimes from leaked prototypes, made it one of the most closely watched (and occasionally legally threatened) tech blogs of the 2000s.
Instagram launched iPhone-only in late 2010 and hit 25,000 users on day one. Its web presence stayed minimal for years while the app itself was the whole product.
Shutterfly built its business on printing physical photo books from digital pictures, a bridge business between film photography and today's all-digital photo storage.
